question: How do I register as a new student at ACity?
answer:
New Entrant Registration at ACity has 4 steps:

Step 1 — Complete the health clearance form issued in your admission packet and submit it to the ACity clinic BEFORE or DURING the registration period. You cannot proceed with registration without this.

Step 2 — Make the necessary payments for tuition, hostel, and meal plan. Refer to ACity's fee policy at https://acity.edu.gh/finance-billing/

Step 3 — Submit your registration request online:
a. Go to: https://acityplus.acity.edu.gh/registration-new-student
b. Enter your ACity email address
c. Click 'Find details'

Step 4 — You will receive an email from the Registry confirming your registration, listing your assigned courses, and confirming issuance of your ID card with your name, photo, roll number, and programme.

IMPORTANT: A student who fails to register for a semester or a course shall forfeit that semester or course. Registration deadlines are communicated via email and on the academic calendar at https://acity.edu.gh

Contact: registry@acity.edu.gh

question: What is the Medical Certificate for ACity and where do I get it?
answer:
The ACity Medical Certificate is a form that must be completed by a MEDICAL OFFICER at any government or accredited hospital. It includes:
• Your personal details and medical history
• Checks for: allergies, G6PD, vision, blood pressure, hearing, heart, lungs, haemoglobin, sickling, abdomen, extremities
• A declaration that you are: (a) medically fit, or (b) medically fit but with a condition requiring special attention

Download the form here:
https://acity.edu.gh/downloads/admissions-packet/health-form-medical-certification.pdf

Bring the COMPLETED and SIGNED form (with doctor's stamp) when you report to campus on registration day. Also attach:
• Copy of your NHIS card or Private Medical Insurance Card
• Doctor's note explaining any medical conditions
• Copy of toxicology screening/test report

question: Can overnight visitors stay in the ACity hostel?
answer:
Overnight visitors ARE allowed but with strict conditions:

1. You must get written permission from the SCA office via email BEFORE the visit
2. The visitor must sign in AND out with the Hostel Coordinator and leave a form of ID
3. A visitor may stay overnight for a MAXIMUM of 1 night over any 2-week period
4. You may NOT have more than one overnight visitor at a time
5. Non-residents are NOT allowed to shower in the hostel

General visitor rules:
• All guests must be met in the hostel lobby and sign in with the hostel coordinator, leaving an ID
• Visitors (non-students, friends, relatives) are NOT allowed in the hostel after 9pm — non-negotiable
• Violation of the 9pm rule: Temporary Hostel Ban (1st offense), Permanent Hostel Ban (repeat)
• If a visitor misbehaves, action may be taken against the student who invited them

Contact: sca@acity.edu.gh
keywords: overnight visitors, hostel guests, visitor policy, 9pm rule, overnight stay hostel

question: Can I stay in the ACity hostel during school vacations?
answer:
Generally NO — all hostel residents must vacate the hostel during school breaks and vacations, emptying their rooms completely.

Exceptions:
• You may stay if you are taking courses during the break
• You may stay if an end-of-semester project or exam due date has been extended
• All students get up to ONE WEEK after exams to prepare and vacate

If you need to stay during break, the Director of Finance will determine a fee to be paid.

For international students living outside Ghana:
• Make a written request to the SCA Department if you need to arrive a day early or depart a day after closure
• Approval is case-by-case and only after receiving written permission

Contact: sca@acity.edu.gh

question: What are the AC temperature settings in ACity hostel rooms?
answer:
ACity has implemented Sensibo Sky AC Sensors in hostel rooms for energy efficiency. The sensors enforce the following temperature range:

• Minimum: 21°C
• Maximum: 25°C

Students must NOT tamper with, remove, disable, or cover the AC sensor. Tampering includes:
• Physically removing or damaging the device
• Covering or obstructing the sensor
• Disconnecting it from power or Wi-Fi
• Attempting to reset or reconfigure it

Penalty for tampering: Charged DOUBLE the full replacement cost of the sensor + possible disciplinary action.

question: What is the procedure for international students coming to ACity? How do I legalize my stay in Ghana?
answer:
International Student Procedures — Steps to regularize your stay in Ghana:

STEP 1 — Non-Citizenship Card (within 20 days of arrival):
• You need: USD 120 + your international passport
1. Visit the National Identification Authority (NIA) at Ghana Immigration Service with your passport
2. NIA captures your bio data and issues your Non-Citizenship Card
3. Pay USD 120 fee
4. Photo your card and passport — email to yourself for safekeeping
5. File a hard copy at ACity Registry
6. Registry issues your Introductory Letter for your Residence Permit
NB: Renew NIA card annually for USD 60

STEP 2 — Residence Permit (within 25 days of arrival):
Documents needed:
• Introductory letter from Registry
• Photocopy of admission offer letter
• Photocopy of fee payment receipts
• Campus address: Digital GPS: Academic City College, GE-189-4636 ECOWAS Highway | Postal: PO Box AD 421, Adabraka-Accra
• International passport + photocopy of NIA card
• 2 passport-sized photos
• Residence Permit fees:
  - ECOWAS (without Ghana card): GHS 500 | with Ghana card: GHS 400
  - Non-ECOWAS (without Ghana card): GHS 560 | with Ghana card: GHS 460
  - Administrative fee (all applicants): GHS 200

Processing options:
• Go to Ghana Immigration Service (GIS), North Ridge + pay at their banking hall (takes 4 weeks), OR
• Submit all documents to the SCA office by the deadline they communicate via email

Late penalty: ECOWAS GHS 200/month | Non-ECOWAS GHS 300/month

question: What is the GTEC Equivalency Letter and how do international students get it?
answer:
The GTEC (Ghana Tertiary Education Commission) Equivalency Letter verifies that your foreign academic certificates are equivalent to Ghanaian standards. ALL foreign certificates — EXCEPT WASSCE — must be verified by GTEC.

What you need:
• Original results/certificates (any in foreign languages must be translated into English)
• Proof of identification
• GTEC prescribed fees

Steps:
1. Visit the GTEC office with the above documents
2. Pay the prescribed fee and submit documents
3. GTEC will send the Equivalency Letter directly to Academic City University

question: What is the residence permit penalty for overstaying in Ghana as a student?
answer:
If you overstay in Ghana without processing a Residence Permit, or if your permit expires without renewal, penalties are:

• ECOWAS nationals: GHS 200 per month of overstay
• Non-ECOWAS/Foreign nationals: GHS 300 per month of overstay

Process your Residence Permit within 25 days of arrival to avoid penalties. Contact sca@acity.edu.gh for assistance.

question: What medical history information does ACity collect from students?
answer:
As part of the health clearance process, ACity collects your medical history including whether you have or have had:
• Epilepsy/seizures, Sickle Cell, Asthma, Diabetes
• Psychological conditions, High blood pressure/cardiovascular problems
• Fainting spells, Severe allergies, Headaches, Depression
• Digestive problems/ulcers, Ear/nose/throat problems
• Anaemia/blood disorders, Back/musculoskeletal problems
• Any medications you should NOT be administered
• Immunisation records: Measles & Rubella, Yellow Fever, Chicken Pox, Covid-19

This information is CONFIDENTIAL — only medical staff, the Office of Student Affairs, and Executives have access.
